---
title: "Using Q-CRAFT from Python"
subtitle: "Teal Insights' scriptable counterpart to the IMF Q-CRAFT workbook"
---

Q-CRAFT (2024-11-15) is Teal Insights' Python package for the IMF Quantitative Climate Risk Assessment Fiscal Tool, workbook vintage 2024-11-15. It lets an economist rerun that workbook's baseline and climate scenarios from code, with the assumptions named next to the result.

The calculation is a partial-equilibrium scenario. Country data and assumptions for demography, labour productivity, inflation, and interest rates produce a baseline through 2099. Climate scenarios then apply empirical temperature effects to that path and trace the fiscal consequences. A result holds for the assumptions you pass in. Report those assumptions with the numbers.

Teal Insights publishes this package. The methodology and the workbook are the IMF's. Reuse does not imply IMF endorsement.

## Installation

```bash
uv add "qcraft-2024-11-15 @ git+https://github.com/Teal-Insights/qcraft-2024-11-15"
```

Public calculations live in `qcraft.api`. Each one takes a single `*Inputs` object. Build that object with `from_defaults(...)`: omitted leaves stay at the values stored in this workbook vintage, and the keyword arguments you pass replace them.

```{python}
from qcraft import BaselinePopulationGrowthInputs
from qcraft.api import compute_baseline_population_growth

population_growth = compute_baseline_population_growth(
    BaselinePopulationGrowthInputs.from_defaults(country="France")
)
(
    population_growth.domain.axes[0].keys[0],
    population_growth.domain.axes[0].keys[-1],
    population_growth[2099],
)
```

`country="France"` is the only override in that call. Productivity, inflation, the interest-rate mode, the fiscal rule, the debt target, and expenditure rigidity stay at the vintage's stored dashboard values. The workbook's default country is Afghanistan, so those stored values are Afghanistan's dashboard settings. Replace any setting that does not belong in the analysis.

Annual results are immutable named-axis series. Inspect `.domain.axes` for the year and scenario keys, iterate `.items()` for coordinate/value pairs, and select a scenario with `.sel(SCENARIO=...)`.

## What a run is for

Use a run to compare long-term fiscal pressure under alternative assumptions, and to see how a climate path changes debt relative to the baseline you chose. The [methodology page](user-guide/methodology-and-interpretation.qmd) explains the identities behind those comparisons.

Adaptation spending, disaster GDP losses, sea-level rise, monetary conditions, external balances, and the GDP effects of fiscal consolidation sit outside the calculation. Discrete revenue and expenditure shocks can be entered on their own; the package leaves their GDP effects unmodelled.
